A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebArena and VisualWebArena experiments, search-parameter ablations, trajectory-reranking results, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds value-function ablations, additional agent configurations, and an expanded reranking experiment.

M1.justification: The proposed search procedure remains unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly stores values alongside frontier states, matching the rule already given in v1 Section 3.3. Additional backbone and evaluator experiments instantiate the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 910 VisualWebArena and 812 WebArena tasks and retain the 200-task VisualWebArena ablation subset. Additional models and trajectory budgets do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ICAL as a published VisualWebArena comparator, reporting 23.4%, and a no-search Llama-3 baseline on WebArena. Table 8 adds Llama-3.1 and GPT-4o-mini baseline pairs. The existing reranker remains; removing the duplicate GPT-4o row does not remove a comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds experimental configurations using LLaVA, ground-truth rewards, and different self-consistency sample counts, plus additional agent backbones. Reranking expands from three trajectories to a one-through-seven sweep. The original datasets, evaluation metric, search settings, and action limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds substantive tests of alternative value functions, oracle rewards, and self-consistency. Appendix A.2.1 examines additional agent/evaluator pairings. The existing reranking analysis moves to Appendix A.2.2 and expands beyond three trajectories. These additions substantially strengthen analysis of the method's components and generality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Self-consistency samples and reranked trajectories are inference settings, not repeated evaluations for uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original headline rates of 26.4% on VisualWebArena and 19.2% on WebArena remain. New results include the value-function ablations in Table 4, Llama-3 WebArena results, and additional model pairings in Table 8. The expanded reranking curve retains 28.5% at three trajectories; Figure 6 plots 31% at seven, although the accompanying text reports 30%.

T1.justification: The environment assumptions, state and reward definitions, and value-function equations are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears. The pseudocode correction restates the existing frontier-update rule.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about environment-grounded search, compatibility with existing agents, benchmark improvements, and scaling with inference compute. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 removes the attribution of Llama-3's gains to the stronger GPT-4o evaluator. It interprets the new ablations as showing headroom from better value functions and reduced evaluation noise through self-consistency. The new ethics statement explicitly limits intended use to research; existing practical limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies zero-shot, current-observation prompting for LLaVA and documents an open-weight Llama-3/LLaVA configuration. It clarifies the frontier entries in Algorithm 1 and explicitly mentions experiment launch scripts in the reproducibility statement. Existing prompts, core implementation settings, and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to the Llama 3 model report, LLaVA-NeXT, ICAL, and Agent Workflow Memory. Section 2.2 briefly incorporates ICAL and AWM into the related-work discussion, while the main novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local prose edits, organizes agent descriptions by input format, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, and reorganizes the appendix around additional ablations. Most of the narrative and the detailed prompts remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 8 and the reranking plot in Figure 6, reformats Table 2, and correctly labels the retained depth/breadth display as Table 3. Existing qualitative figures and prompt displays are retained, with some relocation and renumbering; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the value-function and self-consistency ablations, open-weight configuration, and broader reranking comparison provide better validation and reproducibility support for the existing method. These are useful extensions of an already established empirical study. The new reranking discrepancy between the text's 30% and Figure 6's 31% is a limited reporting weakness.
